title: Matcha white chocolate bark
subtitle: white chocolate with matcha stirred through and set into a thin, breakable slab
excerpt: Matcha white chocolate bark is melted white chocolate with matcha powder stirred through and poured onto a lined tray to set to a thin slab. The slight bitterness of matcha cuts against the sweetness of white chocolate and gives the bark a vivid pale green colour. The tray goes into the fridge for 30 minutes before the bark is broken into irregular pieces.
sourceNotes: Chocolate bark as a confection documented in American and British home baking from the late twentieth century. Matcha and white chocolate as a flavour pairing became popular in British baking from the 2010s onward, following the spread of Japanese pastry influence.

glossaryTerms.definition: The process of heating and cooling chocolate to specific temperatures to stabilise the cocoa butter crystals. Properly tempered chocolate sets with a glossy finish and a clean snap. Bark does not need full tempering; the fridge sets it firm enough.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in a cool, dry place in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Store away from direct sunlight to prevent fat bloom.

content.text: Matcha white chocolate bark is white chocolate melted and stirred with matcha powder before pouring onto a lined tray to set. The matcha cuts the sweetness of the white chocolate and gives the slab a clean, slightly bitter green note. The bark does not need full
; setting it in the fridge firms it enough to break cleanly.
Melt the white chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring gently until smooth. Do not let the bowl touch the water. Remove from the heat.

Sift the matcha powder over the melted chocolate. Stir until the matcha is fully incorporated and the chocolate is an even pale green. Work out any lumps of matcha by pressing them against the side of the bowl.
Line a baking tray with baking paper. Pour the matcha chocolate onto the tray and spread to about 5 mm thick with a spatula. Scatter sesame seeds over the top if using.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes until fully set. Remove and break into irregular pieces by hand.

attrs.problem: White chocolate seized into a stiff, grainy paste
attrs.avoid: Avoid any water getting into the melting chocolate; even a drop will cause it to seize.
attrs.fix: Ensure the bowl and spatula are completely dry before starting. If the chocolate seizes, it cannot be rescued for this recipe but can be used in a biscuit dough or cake batter.

attrs.problem: Matcha lumps visible in the finished bark
attrs.avoid: Avoid adding matcha straight from the tin without sifting; it clumps in melted chocolate.
attrs.fix: Sift the matcha powder before adding it, and stir slowly and thoroughly. Press any remaining lumps against the side of the bowl with the spatula before spreading.
